penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: AI upskilling curricula target individual learners; at $99-499/seat, the model needs hundreds to thousands of paying consumers to generate meaningful revenue, pushing this firmly into b2c-at-scale territory.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Educational content generates questions, curriculum feedback requests, and progress-tracking needs that Claude can partly handle but will require ongoing curation and human judgment for quality maintenance.

rationale: The buyers here are individual freelancers and career-switchers — a broad, heterogeneous consumer audience who already have free alternatives (YouTube, free Coursera audits, HN itself) and whose willingness to pay is real but price-sensitive and fragmented. The HN thread has 13 points and 15 comments, which is a weak signal; this is not a specific business buyer with a budget line. Operational autonomy is the core problem: a living AI-skills curriculum requires frequent content updates as the LLM landscape shifts weekly, meaning Youval would be doing ongoing editorial work per customer cohort — not autonomous delivery. The b2c-at-scale penalty reflects that this only works as a business at volume the solo factory cannot reach without heavy marketing spend.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build at this stage. If revisited: the micro-service would be a drip-email AI skills curriculum (Claude-generated, weekly lessons) sold via a Stripe subscription page. The factory would auto-generate and schedule lesson emails through Claude prompts. Sales channel would be HN 'Show HN' posts and Twitter/X outreach — but reaching enough paying customers as a solo operator without an audience is the real blocker. Support and billing could be mostly automated, but curriculum quality drift would require recurring operator involvement. A solo non-technical operator could technically launch this, but sustaining meaningful revenue without an existing audience or marketing budget makes this a poor fit for the factory's model.
notes: Fails buyer_clarity gate (score 4 < floor 6) and operational_autonomy gate (score 4 < floor 7). Even if total were higher, both build gates would cap stage at validate. b2c_at_scale_needed penalty reflects the volume dependency.
